one_line: Security triage and capacity-aware remediation planning with human-controlled agent assistance.
what_it_does: Outpost organizes fictional security findings, evidence, prioritization, remediation sprints, notes, locks, and provenance in a shared analyst/agent workspace.
leverage_rationale: Typed tools operate on structured findings, risk summaries, comparisons, and sprint plans in the same state as the analyst UI; pixel automation would be substantially less reliable for consequential triage.
leverage_evidence: About text describes fourteen schema-validated browser-native tools.
Human and agent actions modify the same visible findings and remediation state.
Frame sheet shows a coherent findings/remediation dashboard, though not a readable tool trace.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a polished, intentionally scoped security workspace with multiple coordinated surfaces and a visible remediation board; the frame sheet supports product existence but not every end-to-end operation.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet shows branded dashboard, risk metrics, finding cards, and remediation-plan layout.
Description specifies findings, locks, undo, activity provenance, and capacity-aware sprint behavior.
Demo is reported alive and has a public repository.
impact_rationale: Security teams have a real prioritization and limited-capacity problem, and explainable triage with human locks addresses trust and operational constraints directly.
impact_evidence: Description targets analysts handling many defensive findings with limited engineering time.
Risk-to-effort five-day sprint and provenance trail align with real security operations.
Frame sheet visibly presents a finding/remediation workflow.
creativity_rationale: The human-judgment/agent-speed division, capacity-aware remediation planning, and provenance-first workflow are a fresh synthesis beyond a generic security dashboard.
creativity_evidence: Human lock on consequential severity/status decisions.
Agent-assisted reprioritization and risk-to-effort planning.
Provenance separates human, agent, and system actions.
usability_note: Clear dashboard and board metaphor; dense security information may require onboarding.
red_flags: Frame sheet does not visibly prove a live agent invocation or complete remediation run.
standouts: Strong shared-state governance model and unusually concrete capacity-aware planning.
advance_reason: High-quality, credible security workflow with strong WebMCP leverage and visible product execution.

one_line: An agent-first data-labeling studio where agents annotate and humans review.
what_it_does: YADL provides projects and annotation workflows for boxes, polygons, keypoints, media, augmentation, and export through browser-native tools.
leverage_rationale: Semantic annotation tools let an agent label visual data directly instead of clicking thousands of boxes; structured geometry and commit/export are central to the product.
leverage_evidence: About text reports roughly thirty WebMCP tools for project, Studio, navigation, geometry editing, and commits/exports.
The stated model is agent labels while a human reviews.
Frame sheet shows a media/labeling workspace and evolving agent-oriented interface.
execution_rationale: The packet describes a substantial full-stack labeling product and reports a continuous 1,500-label run, but the frame sheet is visually small and does not clearly show annotation completion end-to-end.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet shows a dark labeling/workbench UI with media previews and controls.
Description names Next.js, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, S3, durable augmentation, and export.
Reported 1,500 direct labels and 0.99 Macro-F1 provide outcome evidence, though self-reported.
impact_rationale: Computer-vision teams have a severe labeling bottleneck; reliable agent-produced annotations with human review could create direct productivity and dataset-quality value.
impact_evidence: Description explicitly targets costly manual computer-vision labeling.
Supports multiple annotation primitives and durable jobs.
Reported large continuous labeling run and strong evaluation result.
creativity_rationale: The agent-labels/human-reviews inversion and sign-language control-plane demonstration are notably ambitious and memorable.
creativity_evidence: Agent performs annotation while reviewer retains oversight.
Codex Micro keyboard interpretation via sign language.
Combines multimodal labeling, augmentation, and WebMCP semantics.
usability_note: Agent-first workflow can remove repetitive work, but the dense studio and review burden remain complex.
red_flags: Frame sheet does not make named tool calls or final annotation export legible.
standouts: Transformative fit between structured WebMCP geometry operations and high-volume labeling.
advance_reason: Exceptional leverage and real audience need; evidence supports a serious product despite limited legibility of the motion frames.

one_line: A shared tabletop text-adventure workspace with a governed AI Co-DM.
what_it_does: Players explore a campaign while a Co-DM agent reads lore and live state, messages players, and proposes high-impact mechanical changes for human approval.
leverage_rationale: The agent receives semantic scene, lore, entity, messaging, and governed-change capabilities against live campaign state; UI-driving would be less precise and less safe for game mechanics.
leverage_evidence: Five browser-native tools cover scene inspection, world search, entity inspection, messaging, and proposals.
High-impact changes remain queued for human DM approval.
Frame sheet shows a dark campaign/console workflow with task and player-facing surfaces.
execution_rationale: The description specifies a coherent player/DM/agent architecture with real-time state, authorization, schemas, bounded search, and audit receipts; frames support the product surface.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet shows browser-based campaign/task UI and a console-like interaction state.
Description identifies ASP.NET Core/PostgreSQL engine, SignalR player/DM views, and server authorization.
Demo is reported alive.
impact_rationale: Tabletop groups have a real desire for responsive storytelling and campaign continuity; the product preserves human DM authority while expanding capacity.
impact_evidence: Shared workspace serves players, human DMs, and agents.
Lore-aware reactions and player messaging address common campaign-management friction.
Approval boundary fits the social and consequential nature of game state.
creativity_rationale: A governed Co-DM for a live text-adventure campaign is a memorable interaction model, pursued with lore, mechanics, messaging, and accountability rather than generic chat.
creativity_evidence: Agent proposes consequences while DM remains authority.
Combines old-school text adventure with live agent collaboration.
Explicit distinction between inspection and approved mechanical intervention.
usability_note: Natural-language play is approachable; DM governance adds useful but necessary friction.
red_flags: Frame sheet does not clearly expose a named invocation or completed proposal approval.
standouts: Strongly differentiated Co-DM governance and shared campaign state.
advance_reason: Creative, credible game experience where semantic agent access materially improves the intended collaboration.

one_line: A recovery contract that lets agents resume failed workflows without replaying successful side effects.
what_it_does: Kenny journals an onboarding workflow, classifies preserved/recovered/blocked steps, proposes alternatives, and selectively resumes after human approval.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP exposes structured recovery state and selective-resume semantics directly to an external agent; generic UI automation cannot safely infer idempotency and irreversible boundaries.
leverage_evidence: Six tools cover onboarding state, recovery plan, slot search, proposal, and resume.
The workflow explicitly preserves four successful actions and avoids replay.
No agent approval tool leaves consequential authorization in the webpage UI.
execution_rationale: The deterministic partial-failure demo is tightly scoped and technically coherent, with a clear failure, recovery plan, approval gate, and resume behavior.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet shows the Kenny workflow page and multiple onboarding steps.
Description gives a concrete five-step scenario and expected recovery outcome.
Uses append-only journal, idempotency, local persistence, and deterministic simulated services.
impact_rationale: Partial failure in multi-step automation is a real operational and safety problem; preserving valid work while recovering only the failed step has broad practical value.
impact_evidence: Employee onboarding example includes accounts, license, laptop, and orientation booking.
Explicitly prevents repeated completed actions and blocks irreversible email pending approval.
Protocol-independent recovery core could generalize beyond the demo.
creativity_rationale: The preserve/recover/block contract and selective resume are an original, deeply pursued answer to a neglected agent reliability problem.
creativity_evidence: Recovery semantics are application-declared rather than guessed by the agent.
Human approval is deliberately kept outside WebMCP.
Clear journaling and idempotency model turns failure handling into the product.
usability_note: The state taxonomy makes complex recovery understandable, though workflow concepts are technical.
red_flags: Frames show the workflow UI but not a legible tool trace or final resumed state.
standouts: Best-defined reliability contribution: no replay of successful side effects.
advance_reason: Exceptional WebMCP leverage, high practical impact, and a sharply differentiated reliability contract.

one_line: Pull requests for application state: co-design, simulate, diff, and govern workflows.
what_it_does: ProcessTwin lets humans edit process graphs while agents read and modify semantic scenarios, validate, simulate, and return diffs for human application.
leverage_rationale: Semantic graph edits, validation, simulation, forks, and diffs are exactly the operations that pixel-driven canvas automation handles poorly; shared state and human merge are central.
leverage_evidence: Description contrasts three domain-level calls with long sequences of drags/clicks.
Agent receives structured graphs, validation, percentiles, bottlenecks, and fixes.
Private scenarios and before/after diffs are surfaced without an agent merge tool.
execution_rationale: The product has a coherent process-editor/simulator/governance loop and visible telemetry, though the frame text is too small to verify all simulation outcomes.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet shows a dark workflow/developer interface transitioning to console-like execution output.
Description specifies versioning, actor attribution, boundaries, validation, simulation, and telemetry.
Public repository and submitted video support implementation credibility.
impact_rationale: Teams designing operational workflows need safer experimentation and reviewable changes; process simulation plus human-controlled application directly addresses that need.
impact_evidence: Targets workflow editors where semantic correctness matters.
Simulation percentiles, bottlenecks, and suggested fixes provide actionable analysis.
Human reviews scenario diffs before applying to live process.
creativity_rationale: Applying pull-request semantics to live application/process state is a novel interaction model with ambitious governance and simulation depth.
creativity_evidence: Process-state pull requests and private scenario forks.
Telemetry quantifies UI work avoided.
Explicitly omits agent merge to preserve human governance.
usability_note: Semantic operations and diffs reduce canvas friction; process modeling remains inherently specialized.
red_flags: Exact tool call/result text is not legible in the frame sheet.
standouts: Excellent translation of code-review governance into workflow-state editing.
advance_reason: Transformative leverage and strong impact/creativity with a credible, coherent product loop.

one_line: An adaptive camera storefront where agent requests visibly reshape one shared commerce canvas.
what_it_does: ShopCanvas exposes product search, inspection, comparison, review filtering, and mock-cart updates while highlighting each agent action in stable bento cells.
leverage_rationale: Structured product and cart tools make comparison and filtering more reliable and keep results visible, but a competent general agent could achieve much of the same commerce outcome with UI interaction.
leverage_evidence: Five imperative tools are named: search_products, inspect_product, compare_products, show_reviews, set_cart_quantity.
Stable mounted cells visibly acknowledge and highlight tool effects.
Frame sheet explicitly shows the agent calling search_products for a budget request.
execution_rationale: The visual system is polished and intentionally designed around stable layout, accessible announcements, and visible tool effects; the frame sheet shows catalog and Monitor AI states.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet shows camera catalog, adaptive workspace, and Monitor AI panel.
Named search action and resulting catalog context are visible.
Description addresses mounted cells, animation, and live-region accessibility.
impact_rationale: Shoppers benefit from reduced context switching and clearer comparison, though the fictional catalog and mock cart limit demonstrated real-world depth.
impact_evidence: Targets common product research friction across specs, reviews, comparison, and cart.
Single shared surface keeps the original request and visual response together.
Camera catalog provides a concrete shopping scenario.
creativity_rationale: The conversational storefront and stable adaptive bento interaction are a fresh synthesis, though commerce search itself is familiar.
creativity_evidence: Every request produces an understandable visual response on one surface.
Cells expand without teleporting or reordering.
Agent activity remains visible rather than hidden in chat.
usability_note: Strong visual continuity and accessible announcements make agent changes easy to follow.
red_flags: Demo uses a fictional catalog and local mock cart; demo_alive is unknown.
standouts: Most legible direct tool invocation and result transition in the packet.
advance_reason: Clear, polished, well-evidenced demonstration of visible agent actions in commerce.

one_line: A local-first registry that turns reviewed action packs into safe WebMCP tools inside existing signed-in sessions.
what_it_does: Agentready Network binds declarative, origin-scoped action packs to a user’s session, projects bounded untrusted output, and requires human authority for writes.
leverage_rationale: The product addresses the central adoption barrier: structured agent access to sites without vendor APIs, using the existing authenticated tab and reviewed tools rather than screenshot guessing.
leverage_evidence: Description reframes the signed-in tab as a typed, narrow API.
Origin/fingerprint binding, drift fail-closed, declarative manifests, bounded output, and human write authority are core behavior.
Frame sheet communicates the login-versus-screenshot gap and WebMCP adoption concept.
execution_rationale: The architecture and safety model are unusually well specified, but the frame sheet is primarily conceptual/marketing and does not visibly prove a complete live pack execution.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet shows the product narrative, metric cards, and WebMCP concept.
Description details registry/runtime, reviewed fingerprints, allowlist projection, and consent boundaries.
Public repository and live demo are reported.
impact_rationale: If reliable, this solves a broad and concrete problem for operations teams trapped in sites without APIs while preserving the user’s existing permissions and oversight.
impact_evidence: Targets monitoring, scheduling, payer, vendor, and admin sites lacking APIs.
Uses existing login rather than requiring vendor adoption.
Safety controls address credential, drift, and untrusted-output risks.
creativity_rationale: User-adopted action packs that safely convert authenticated web sessions into agent surfaces are a highly original adoption and governance model.
creativity_evidence: Adoption is inverted from vendor integration to reviewed user-owned packs.
Declarative-never-executable registry is a distinctive safety constraint.
Human authorization and receipts are integrated into the concept.
usability_note: Powerful for technical operators, but pack review, origin binding, and drift handling add setup complexity.
red_flags: Video frames are conceptual and do not clearly show a live action-pack invocation or result.
standouts: Ambitious, safety-conscious answer to the no-API adoption problem.
advance_reason: Exceptional concept, impact, and leverage; execution confidence is moderated by thin direct motion evidence.

one_line: A collaborative whiteboard where the agent reads and edits the live graph with state-dependent tools.
what_it_does: The Excalidraw-based board exposes note, shape, diagram, list, and connection tools whose availability changes with board state and shares undo/state with human drawing.
leverage_rationale: Agents receive the board’s semantic graph and state-dependent capabilities instead of screenshots; dynamic registration and shared undo make the integration materially more reliable than pixel driving.
leverage_evidence: Description says the agent reads the graph and creates diagrams from board content in one call.
Tool list changes when elements or two-plus shapes exist.
Agent and human edits share canvas state and one undo history.
execution_rationale: The packet gives a coherent implementation with shared canvas functions, Zod contracts, AbortController lifecycle, and a visible whiteboard demo, though the frame sheet itself is low-detail.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet shows browser whiteboard/workspace states and conversational composer transitions.
Description names React, Vite, Excalidraw, Cloudflare Workers, and runtime schema validation.
Dynamic registration and teardown address a real lifecycle requirement.
impact_rationale: Teams and individuals regularly need to turn rough visual thinking into structured diagrams; an agent that joins the board can remove translation friction while preserving human control.
impact_evidence: Use case starts from sticky notes and asks agent to draw user-flow steps.
No install, configuration, or API key lowers access friction.
Shared undo supports safe collaborative editing.
creativity_rationale: A board whose agent tool surface changes with live board state is a distinctive interaction model and a strong use of page-local WebMCP semantics.
creativity_evidence: State-dependent tool registration is central, not cosmetic.
Agent joins the board rather than returning a detached image.
Same contracts generate schemas and validate runtime arguments.
usability_note: Familiar whiteboard interaction plus no-install agent participation is approachable; diagram generation still needs review.
red_flags: Frame sheet does not make a named tool call or generated diagram fully legible.
standouts: Dynamic, board-state-dependent tool surface is a particularly strong WebMCP-native idea.
advance_reason: Distinctive WebMCP interaction model with credible implementation and meaningful collaborative value.

one_line: A culturally grounded African dream-interpretation platform with safe agent access to specialist context.
what_it_does: Amaphupho offers dream interpretation, an African dream-symbol glossary, and a community circle, exposing structured capabilities to compatible agents.
leverage_rationale: Structured specialist tools can provide an agent with culturally grounded interpretation and glossary context, but the demonstrated user outcome remains achievable through ordinary website interaction with some friction.
leverage_evidence: Description frames the agent as knowing the person while Amaphupho knows the specialist cultural domain.
Three structured tools are exposed, including interpretation and glossary access.
Frame sheet shows the real product landing page and interpretation call-to-action, but not a clear tool trace.
execution_rationale: The packet shows a complete branded product with dark/light themes, interpreter, glossary, community feed, and a reported live task toast; frame evidence primarily shows the landing page.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet clearly shows Sangoma AI Dream Interpretation landing UI and navigation.
Description lists multiple coherent product areas and production UI.
Demo is reported alive with public repository and many gallery images.
impact_rationale: There is credible value for people seeking culturally respectful reflection and community context, provided the product remains an interpretive aid rather than authority.
impact_evidence: Explicitly targets flattening and omission of African dream traditions.
Guest interpreter and glossary lower access barriers.
Community circle supports shared cultural meaning-making.
creativity_rationale: The culturally grounded specialist-domain framing and separation between general agent context and local cultural knowledge are original and meaningful.
creativity_evidence: Southern African Zulu, Xhosa, and Sotho perspectives are foregrounded.
Agent/platform division preserves specialist context.
Combines interpretation, glossary, and community rather than generic chatbot output.
usability_note: Atmospheric, clear landing page and guest flow; culturally sensitive interpretation needs careful expectation-setting.
red_flags: Frame sheet does not clearly show a completed interpretation result or named invocation.
standouts: Strong cultural specificity and responsible framing of AI as interpretive rather than authoritative.
advance_reason: Distinctive culturally grounded product with credible audience value and solid execution evidence.

one_line: A living museum record where agents research and draft, while curators decide what becomes official.
what_it_does: RE:TURN presents objects with provenance gaps, accepts community evidence with publication controls, and lets curator agents compare records and draft labels for human review.
leverage_rationale: Agents can structure provenance research, compare submissions, and draft timelines/labels against shared records, while the human curator retains publication authority; semantic access is much safer than scraping or UI guessing.
leverage_evidence: Description specifies agent comparison, timeline construction, and label drafting.
Research is free but official record changes require a curator.
Frame sheet shows object detail, archival presentation, assistant panel, and full-demo transition, though no legible invocation.
execution_rationale: The product has a coherent museum workflow, clear submission privacy choices, provenance gaps, curator inbox, and a strong visual identity; the frame sheet demonstrates multiple composed surfaces.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet shows RE:TURN branding, Moonbird Mask record, assistant panel, and full landing page.
Description specifies eight objects, timelines, gaps, submissions, curator inbox, and draft workflow.
Demo is reported alive with multiple gallery images.
impact_rationale: Museums and communities have a real provenance and representation problem; accountable community contributions can preserve knowledge without letting automation overwrite authority.
impact_evidence: Targets missing provenance, copied labels, and community knowledge stranded in inboxes.
Submitters choose public, anonymous, or private handling.
Curator review prevents agent-generated history from becoming official automatically.
creativity_rationale: Treating museum records as living, contested documents and formalizing agent research beneath curator authority is a memorable, ambitious interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Labels visibly expose gaps rather than smoothing them over.
Community evidence sits beside official records until verified.
WebMCP is used for research assistance without delegating historical authority.
usability_note: Editorial object pages and explicit contribution controls are approachable; curator workflows are more specialized.
red_flags: Frame sheet suggests assistant activity but does not show a readable tool call or completed draft publication flow.
standouts: Excellent ethical boundary: agents assist reconstruction but cannot decide official history.
advance_reason: High-impact, creative museum workflow with strong governance and credible product evidence.
